why: One transient provider failure makes the four-game cohort invalid. The three completed, identity-pinned games beat random legal play by only 5.8% on mean score, below the 10% development threshold and without enough games for a meaningful positive uncertainty bound. Together with Sonnet's valid four-game failure, this does not prove that extra language-model capability improves the character-only task.
next: Do not run the 30-seed admission suite and do not train a 30–50M 2048 specialist. Preserve these traces as negative evidence and move the capability-gradient experiment to a benchmark with a verifiable intelligence advantage over its legal random baseline.
limitations: The Opus cohort is incomplete, so its partial comparison is directional evidence rather than a valid score.
The 32-move cap is a screening ruler, not a full game or frozen admission suite.
This rejects the current character-only formulation, not every possible textual or visual formulation of 2048.
